help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:146  answers, and only the first is a healthy one:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:147  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:148  * last run recent and successful -> exit 0
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:149  * last run FAILED -> exit 1, saying which step failed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:150  * no run recorded at all, or nothing has run for longer than
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:151    4x `backup_interval_secs` (minimum 1 hour) -> exit 1. A dead timer
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:152    usually leaves a *successful* last run behind, so this overdue check
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:153    is the only thing that catches it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:154  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:155  Never prints session content: counts, timestamps and digests only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:156  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:157  Default output is a handful of lines and nothing more: the verdict
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:158  above, then aggregate scan counts (per-harness session totals, skipped
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:159  roots, unarchivable-session warning). It stays that size whether the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:160  machine holds three sessions or three thousand, so the verdict never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:161  scrolls away.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:162  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:163  `--sessions` adds the per-session metadata table on top of that —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:164  one line per session (harness / bytes / mtime / first 8 chars of the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:165  id). That is the troubleshooting view; it can be hundreds of lines.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:167  Also print one metadata line per session found (can be hundreds).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:170  Print exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else (the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:171  human lines still go to stderr). Tri-state fields are tagged
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:172  `{"kind":"known",…}` / `{"kind":"unknown","why":…}` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:173  `{"kind":"not_applicable",…}` — an unknown is never serialised as
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:174  `0`, `null` or a missing field. `run_state.kind` is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:175  `known` / `missing` / `unreadable`; `scanner.kind` is `ok` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:176  `failed`. `exit_semantics` documents what the exit code means.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:180  Dump one session back from the repository (sequence-concatenated) and
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:181  print its sha256 for verification — or, with `--all-machines`, merge
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:182  the newest snapshot of every machine and report per-session digests.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:184  Stage directory used by push (mapping into the snapshot tree).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:185  Ignored by `--all-machines`.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:322  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:323  Metadata tier only: this walks snapshot/index/tree objects and never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:324  fetches or decrypts a data blob, which is why it is cheap. On a local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:325  three-session fixture the metadata walk read 11,761 bytes against
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:326  1,206,285 bytes of data packs — two orders of magnitude apart. Use
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:327  `--cost` to see what a full-text pass over the current hits *would*
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:328  cost before asking for one; full-text matching is not implemented.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:329  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:330  One destination per run, always named: there is no automatic merge
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:331  across destinations, and no default destination to search "everything".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:332  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:333  Exit codes distinguish the three answers, because two of them look the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:334  same and mean opposite things: `0` matched something, `1` read the whole
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:335  destination and nothing matched, `3` could not finish reading it — so
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:336  "nothing matched" is unproven. `2` is a usage error, as elsewhere.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:338  Destination to search. Required unless an explicit `--repo` is given.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:374  Binds a short-lived HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` with an OS-assigned port
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:375  (never `0.0.0.0`, never a fixed port), prints the URL, optionally opens
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:376  your browser, and exits when idle or on Ctrl+C. Nothing is installed:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:377  no launchd, no systemd, no background process, no resident daemon.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:378  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:379  THREAT, stated plainly: loopback is NOT a security boundary. Every other
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:380  program running on this machine can connect to `127.0.0.1`, so this is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:381  not "safe because it's local". Access is gated by a random token that is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:382  generated fresh on every launch and appears only in the printed URL —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:383  never in a file, never in a log. Requests without that exact token are
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:384  refused (403), and any method other than GET is refused (405). Treat the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:385  URL as a secret for the lifetime of the process.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:386  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:387  Metadata tier only, same as `search`: machine, first 8 chars of the

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:513  Session id to seal into. Default: the active file's stem.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:516  Maximum sealed shards per bucket (default: 20).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:520  Register this executable as the browsers' Native Messaging host
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:521  (ADR-014 step 2) — or, with `--uninstall`, remove that registration.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:522  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:523  ADR-014 exists because `chrome.downloads` with `saveAs: false` is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:524  overridden by the browser-level "ask where to save each file before
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:525  downloading" preference, which no extension flag can suppress. At up to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:526  200 backfilled conversations a day that is 200 modal dialogs.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:527  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:528  This is one command instead of the five physical actions Native
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:529  Messaging otherwise costs: it renders the host manifest (`name` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:530  `description` / the absolute `path` of *this* executable / `type:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:531  stdio` / the pinned extension allowlist) and drops it into each
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:532  installed browser's discovery directory. No elevation: everything is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:533  per-user.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:534  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:535  Every path written, left alone, skipped or removed is printed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:536  absolutely. "No error" is not the same claim as "a file landed".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:537  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:538  Idempotent: run it twice and there is exactly one manifest per browser,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:539  byte-identical, exit 0 both times. Exit codes: 0 = at least one manifest
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:540  is in place (or, for `--uninstall`, removal finished), 3 = nothing was
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:541  written because no known browser was found, 2 = usage error (bad host
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:542  name / extension id / relative binary path), 1 = an action failed.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:544  Browser to register with, repeatable. Default: every browser whose
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:545  data directory exists on this machine. Naming one explicitly writes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:546  it even when that directory is absent.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:549  Discovery root override (macOS default: `~/Library/Application
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:550  Support`). This is what makes the command testable without writing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:551  into a real browser directory.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:554  Which OS path layout to use. Default: this platform.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:557  Host binary recorded in the manifest. Default: this executable
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:558  (`std::env::current_exe()`), which is the only value that stays
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:559  correct after `cargo install --force`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:562  Host name override. Chromium's grammar is `[a-z0-9_.]` only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:565  Chrome/Chromium/Edge/Brave/Vivaldi extension id.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:568  Firefox add-on id (`browser_specific_settings.gecko.id`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:571  Remove the manifests this command writes — and nothing else.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:574  Windows only: skip the `reg.exe` step and only write the JSON.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:578  The Native Messaging host process itself.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:579  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:580  The framed stdio message loop is NOT implemented in this build. This
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:581  subcommand exists so that the registration above points at something
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:582  verifiable: `--self-test` prints one line of JSON on stdout and exits 0,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:583  which is how "does the host actually start?" is answered on a real
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:584  machine and in later tickets. Without `--self-test` it exits 2 rather
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:585  than pretending to serve a connection.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:586  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:587  Nothing but that one line may ever reach stdout: Chromium reads stdout
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:588  as a `u32` frame length, so a stray log line is read as a multi-gigabyte
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:589  frame and kills the pipe. Diagnostics go to stderr.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:591  Print one line of JSON describing this host, then exit 0.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:595  Build the activity sidecar index for one machine partition (ADR-017).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:596  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:597  Walks `<stage>/sessions/<machine>/<session>/<bucket>/NNNNNN.jsonl`,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:598  concatenates each session's shards in global sequence order, and feeds
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:599  every line through the conversation-time extractor to produce one
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:600  `ActivityRow` per session. The rows are written as JSONL to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:601  `<stage>/meta/<machine>/activity-v1.jsonl` — the file the `overview`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:602  command reads back out of a destination.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:603  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:604  The harness label is inferred from the session directory name: the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:605  canonical archived ids are `<source>.<machine>.<native-id>`, so the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:606  harness is the leading dot-segment (`claude-code.<m>.<uuid>` ->
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:607  `claude-code`); short forms are handled too (`opencode~abc123` ->
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:608  `opencode`, `cursor.d~xxx` -> `cursor`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:609  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:610  Metadata only: the extraction keeps a timestamp per line and throws the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:611  line away. Nothing else about a conversation is ever read, kept or
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:612  printed — the report is counts and the output path only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:613  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:614  Exit codes: `0` = the whole partition was read and the index written;
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:615  `3` = the stage could not be read (or reading was interrupted) — nothing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:616  (complete) was written; `1` = every session was read but the index file
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:617  itself could not be written; `2` = usage error. Same family as
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:618  `collect`/`search`: `3` means "did not finish / never started", `1`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:619  means "finished and then failed".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:621  Stage directory that holds the sealed `sessions/` tree.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:624  Machine partition for `sessions/<machine>/…`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:625  Default: config `machine`, else this machine's identity (generated
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:626  on first use); use `--machine` explicitly to choose the partition.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:630  Write this machine's display-name declaration (ADR-018).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:631  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:632  Writes `<stage>/meta/<machine>/machine.json` — a `MachineDeclaration`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:633  that carries the human display name, the OS and a first-seen time. The
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:634  machine partition is resolved exactly like every other command: config
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:635  `machine` first, then the identity file (generated when missing). The
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:636  next `push` archives the whole stage root, so this file rides along.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:637  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:638  The display name is taken from `--display-name` when given; otherwise
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:639  the system's LocalHostName (`scutil --get LocalHostName` on macOS,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:640  `hostname` elsewhere) is used. If neither is available the field is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:641  written **empty** and the command says so — a name is never invented.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:642  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:643  Exit codes: `0` = the declaration was written; `3` = the machine
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:644  partition could not be resolved or the identity is unusable; `1` = the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:645  file could not be written; `2` = usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:647  Stage directory to write the declaration into (`<stage>/meta/…`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:650  Human display name for this machine. Default: system LocalHostName.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:654  Give a dead or sold machine a display name (ADR-018).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:655  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:656  Writes `<stage>/meta/<target>/label-by-<本机身份>.json` — a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:657  `LabelRecord` expressing *this* machine's opinion about what `<target>`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:658  should be called. It exists for machines that can no longer declare for
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:659  themselves (sold, dead, in a different building). Each file has exactly
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:660  one writer, so concurrent machines never fight over it; the overview
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:661  shows the label with the latest `written_at_unix`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:662  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:663  Exit codes: `0` = the label was written; `3` = the local identity could
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:664  not be resolved; `1` = the file could not be written; `2` = usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:666  Stage directory to write the label into (`<stage>/meta/…`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:669  Machine id (partition) being labelled, e.g. a 32-hex identity.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:672  Display-name override for the target.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:676  Draw the machine × harness activity overview of one destination
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:677  (ADR-017).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:678  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:679  Opens the destination repository, takes each host's newest snapshot
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:680  (the same cross-machine merge as `read --all-machines`), and for every
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:681  snapshot recursively finds the activity index files at
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:682  `meta/<machine>/activity-v1.jsonl`. The paths carry each machine's own
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:683  absolute stage prefix, so they are matched by the trailing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:684  `meta` / `<machine>` / `activity-v1.jsonl` marker — never by a local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:685  path. The indexes are parsed into overview rows and rendered as a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:686  machine × harness matrix, a time-unknown tally and a width-adaptive
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:687  heatmap. Prints counts, machine names and time spans only — never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:688  conversation content.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:689  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:690  A machine that has a snapshot but **no** activity index is listed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:691  explicitly as "索引缺失" — it never vanishes silently, because a missing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:692  index is not the same thing as "that machine had no sessions".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:693  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:694  Exit codes: `0` = at least one index was read and rendered; `1` = the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:695  whole repository was read and there is no activity index at all (a real
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:696  "there is none", not a failure to look); `3` = the repository could not
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:697  be read in full (open / snapshot / tree / dump failure) — the absences
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:698  below are unproven; `2` = usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:700  Destination to open. Required unless an explicit `--repo` is given:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:701  there is no default destination.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:704  Terminal width for the matrix/heatmap (default: 100).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:707  Print exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else (the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:708  human matrix/heatmap is suppressed). Per-session `first_unix` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:709  `last_unix` and `time_source` are tri-state tagged
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:710  `{"kind":"known",…}` / `{"kind":"unknown","why":…}` — an unknown
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:711  time is never `null`. `no_index_anywhere` is `true` on exit 1
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:712  (read in full, no index anywhere); a failed read (exit 3) puts the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:713  reason in `error`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:716  Repository path override.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:719  Masterkey file override.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:722  Concurrency cap override.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:725  Backend option `key=value`, repeatable.
